after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find the largest interval on which the function $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2x+1})$ is continuous.
after.worked_solution:
The function is a composition of two functions, a radical function, and a cosine function.

The cosine is continuous at all points in its domain, and its domain consists of all real numbers. So, we focus on the radical function.

Likewise, the radical function $\sqrt{2x+1}$ is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we set the expression under the radical to be greater than or equal to zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+1\ge 0\,⟹\,2x\ge -1\,⟹\,x\ge -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of $f(x)$ is $[-\frac{1}{2},\infty )$, and the function is continuous on this interval.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find the largest interval of continuity for the function $f(x)={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{x-2}{{5}^{x}}).$
after.worked_solution:
Our function is a logarithmic function, so it is continuous over all points in its domain.

To find the domain of ${log}_{3}⁡(\frac{x-2}{{5}^{x}}),$ we set the expression under the logarithm to be greater than zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-2}{{5}^{x}}>0\,⟹\,x-2>0\,⟹\,x>2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of $f(x)={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{x-2}{{5}^{x}})$ is $(2,\infty ),$ and it is also continuous on this interval.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x+5}{{x}^{2}+2x-15} \\  & =\frac{x+5}{{x}^{2}+5x-3x-15} \\  & =\frac{x+5}{(x+5)(x-3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-3},\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $x\ne -5.$

This function is continuous everywhere except at the excluded points $x=-5$ and $x=3.$
